clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 9949 describes amending provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The order was amended once before its end: Executive Order 10415 of December 2, 1952 struck out "within five years from the date of his transfer to such Board" in the second paragraph and inserted "on or before December 31, 1953"; the clause continued, as amended. The time limit conditions the employee's right and is not shown to end the clause. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9949 at 13 FR 2089 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 17, 1948; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 20, 1948 issue. The register title is Modifying Executive Order No. 9721, Providing for the Transfer of Personnel to Certain Public International Organizations.  Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 1000 to 2347 of the held text, from the authority recital to the direction that the order be published in the Federal Register. It modifies paragraph 3(a) of Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946 for one named employee, Paul D. Miles, on transfer from the Federal Communications Commission to the International Frequency Registration Board of the International Telecommunication Union: he is to have the reemployment rights the parent order gives if his service with that Board is terminated without prejudice within five years of his transfer, in place of the three years the parent order requires, provided he complies with all other provisions of the parent order. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 9949 describes amending provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Later event: Executive Order 10415 of December 2, 1952 (held text, enacting sentence) amends this order by striking out the words "within five years from the date of his transfer to such Board" in its second paragraph and inserting in their place the words "on or before December 31, 1953". It has no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments it is a later event with before and after text, not an end; the modification continued, as amended, until the revocation. Earlier-end check: no end date or termination clause appears in the order; the five-year window, and the fixed date that replaced it, condition the employee's reemployment right and are not an end of the order; no held source shows when or whether the employee transferred. The packet's number search finds this order cited only by Executive Order 10415. The dossier chain names Executive Order 10415 (amendment) and Executive Order 12553 (revocation). Prior research: the dossier shows no canonical prior claim and no conflicting versions. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order without a saving clause; no held source shows that the modification was ever exercised, and the bounded search of the held text of Executive Order 12553, this order's text and the OFR catalog notes shows no residual effect.
